name: Drone aerial
means: The view from a hundred metres up: an oblique or straight-down look across terrain, figures reduced to marks, long raking shadows doing all the modelling, and haze thinning the far distance.
tags: scenery, no humans, bird's-eye view, from above, wide shot, long shadows, distant landscape, atmospheric perspective, highly detailed background
prose: an aerial photograph taken from a drone about a hundred metres up, oblique view down across the landscape, long raking shadows from a low sun, figures and vehicles reduced to small marks, atmospheric haze softening the far distance, deep focus with everything sharp
negative_add: close-up, portrait, eye level, shallow depth of field
works_for: video better than anything else in this set - no anatomy, high altitude, slow parallax, which is exactly the flat static content LTX holds. Inferred, but the reasoning is strong enough to bet on.
note: Be honest about what this is: a CAMERA POSITION, not a rendering idiom, and it overlaps studio/tags/bird's-eye_view.json and shot.cam.height=aerial in VARIABLES.md. That is exactly why it is the one card here marked `either` - the aerial-ness lives in the camera, not the medium, so Animagine draws a perfectly good aerial anime landscape from the tags above. The genuinely weak part on both engines is true nadir: ask for straight down and both drift back to a 30-45 degree oblique. Write `looking straight down, no horizon visible` and then check the render rather than trusting it. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
verdict: Did NOT move the camera up. Still eye level, just a longer street. An aerial is a camera position - a shot property, not a style.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject. studio/_tools/style_examples.py
